_doc: Generator knobs. Every knob is a [easy, hard] pair interpolated by the search's pressure p in [0, 1], then jittered by the mutation step. Costs are in currency at costScale 1 unless keyed salvage.*.

rings._doc: Half extents of the perimeter ring around the core (world units), and sections per side (top/bottom, left/right).

traderRoute._doc: Grid cell, clearance from footprints and walls, and half the gate door opening (world units).

lots._doc: Lots and streets (POLISH-PLAN item 7B): streets of street units cross at the core (its plaza) and repeat every block + street; square lots of block units between them; buildings keep to one lot along each axis they fit.

defendWaves._doc: Swarmlings per wave = swarm knob x share: wave 0 firstShare, then +earlyGrowth per wave; weak raids each come from one attack side; from wave lateFrom on (levels with towers or guards to buy) +lateGrowth per wave, packed at lateGap seconds apart instead of gap, from every attack side. Raiders = swarm x (late)Raiders x wave index. The early raids grow until they drop dropsPerEarlyNeed x the walls and one tower per attack side; then the packed waves grow together until all but the last drop dropsPerNeed x the core of the purchase ladder (walls, the first guards, med bay, and a tower on every socket standing from the start, at their rising prices: Batch 3 sizes the waves against it; tower levels, more guards and later sockets are left to build to the end); each packed wave stays lateStep x the wave before it. With towers or guards to buy there are at least lateFrom + 2 waves. On med bay levels a probe raid (raid) comes through a breach in a quiet side at t s, before the player has scrap to wall it. A defend survive goal lasts surviveTail s past the start of the wave before the last.

scrapHeaps._doc: Batch 3 (Doug): on a share (chance) of defend levels, n scrap heaps (node.salvage_pile, a little scrap each, never regrowing) lie out in the wilds beyond the wall, at least outside units past the ring and within band of that, and roadGap clear of every attack road, so the player scavenges for the first defences.

defendSockets._doc: Batch 3 turret sockets inside the wall at each attack gate (none since Doug's playtest: the road pairs outside are enough): startInside per gate, at spots [u, v] in the gate's frame (u along the wall from the gate's middle, v outward, negative = inside; east and west gates use insideEW, the tower footprint being long along y). A site keeps edge from the (padded) map edge, wallClear from every wall, laneClear from every attack lane and siteR from every station centre; search is how far it may drift from the wanted spot. Gatherables on a socket's tower or pad give way, while more than keepForest ore scrap nodes are left.

defendRoad._doc: Batch 3 (after Kingshot): a defend level's map is padded by pad world units on every side, so each wave walks a long road from the map edge to its gate and the player can run out to meet it. The road out of each attack gate is lined with socket pairs: the first pair v = first units out, then every step (at most maxPairs pairs, endGap short of the edge); a tower stands towerU (towerUEW on an east or west road, the footprint being long along y) to either side of the road with its pad just off it toward the road. The nearest pair stands from the start, pair k opens once k waves have started (the rest with the last wave). Every defence purchase (guard, tower, tower level) raises the next one's price by priceGrowth (the level's pads.defenceGrowth).

terrain._doc: Geography (R3 item 17). chance = share of levels per family that get terrain; pieces = [min, max]; sizes in world units; gaps are clearances to stations, the core, walls, the map edge and the straight lines residents walk.

search._loop: REDESIGN-R3 item 7: reject when the reference bot repeats one player trip (same source type, resource, target; trips a worker already performs are not counted) more than loopCap times in a row. Each reject raises an ease level by 1/loopEaseSteps: hire prices drop up to loopHireCut, core burn slows by up to loopBurnEase, level length shrinks by up to loopLengthCut, start currency grows by up to loopStartCurrency.

humanStars._doc: BACKLOG-R4 Batch 2: stars are earned by the human-view bot (bots HUMAN profile: human reaction, a little error, sees only the screen and the HUD), not the omniscient good bot. Each star objective (challenges and the time target) must be earned on at least minEarned of `seeds` in-level seeds, and at least one seed must take all three stars. 4 of 6 (two thirds) is a star a careful player earns on most attempts without luck or off-screen knowledge; one seed in three may miss it, which keeps the star a challenge. The good bot's old bar was 1 three-star seed in 10. levels:check replays the same seeds and fails a level whose human stars fall more than regressTolerance below the mean recorded at generation (rating.stars.human).
